What Is Swedish Massage?

As a popular form of massage therapy, Swedish massage has been widely practised to help individuals relax, reduce stress and improve circulation. Due to their relaxation purposes, Swedish massage also brings other health benefits such as enhanced mental and physical health, as well as lesser muscle tension. With a wide array of benefits, it is no surprise to see how Swedish massages are adapted in spas to help individuals solve different health conditions.
Benefits of Swedish Massage

Swedish massages have been known as a great therapy to manipulate the muscles and relieve stress or joint pain in the body. It is also suitable for individuals looking to relax and pamper themselves.
Here is a list of health benefits you can expect when you go for a Swedish massage:

1. Stimulates nerves

Regardless of the type of technique you’re opting for, a Swedish massage aims to stimulate blood flow and nerves throughout your body. Through stimulation, your body is less likely to be painful or sore as there is better circulation in your system, overall, reducing any muscle pain and body discomfort as well. If you experience aches and pains across your body such as headaches and even joint pain, this massage will be very helpful for you. A Swedish massage can also provide relief and manage conditions such as fibromyalgia and arthritis.

2. Boost mood

Besides relieving sores and muscles, Swedish massage has proved to improve mood. By stimulating the body, the body will naturally react to enhance the production of dopamine and serotonin – known as chemicals that can increase, pleasure, satisfaction and motivation. Going for a Swedish massage can help to lift your mood, enhance happiness and reduce any forms of stress altogether.

3. Relieve tension

Before every Swedish massage, your body will always be prepped thoroughly with a warm-up. This means that any binding spots and knots in your body are targeted. With applied pressure and techniques, the strokes help to ease the tension of your muscles. This is especially beneficial for individuals who often experience tightness or discomfort in the muscles.

4. Detoxify the body

To avoid the accumulation of lymphatic fluid whenever you’re not moving or using your muscles, Swedish massage can help to better manage the flow of lymphatic drainage. In the long run, your body will be better equipped to flush out any toxins and waste from your body to improve your overall health. You may also achieve a stronger immune system in time.

5. Improve flexibility

By stimulating the muscles and joints, Swedish massage helps you to relax these areas of your body and increase your motion range. Thus, you can expect to see increased stretching capabilities and flexibility.

6. Relaxation

Using rhythmic, long gliding strokes and soothing techniques, Swedish massage can easily trigger your body’s response to relax due to the calming nature of the massage. In time, you’ll notice better sleep quality as your body quickly transitions into a relaxed state. With a relaxed body, you’re better able to cope with stress and anxiety.

7. Improved state of mind

Swedish massage helps to promote a better state of mind as the release of endorphins helps to lower your stress hormones, thus reducing stress and tension. This can lead to better concentration and higher mental clarity and concentration for work.

8. Pampering

If you just want a form of self-pampering massage, Swedish massage is ideal too as it utilises light-to-moderate pressure, to provide you with a relaxing and pampering time.
How Swedish massage Works

To help achieve the health benefits of a Swedish massage, several techniques and hand movements are often combined to stimulate the soft tissues in your body. To help you prepare for your massage session, you’ll first be brought to a private room for preparation and disrobed based on your comfort. But rest assured that you’ll be covered and kept warm throughout your massage.

If there are certain areas of your body you’d wish to highlight to your therapist during the session, feel free to do so and your therapist will allocate more time and varying techniques into treating these areas of concern. For areas that you wish to avoid, you may also advise your therapist accordingly.

• Swedish massage uses kneading, long gliding strokes, deep circular movements and friction to release surface tension.
  • The light-to-moderate pressure is good for relieving light muscle tension and stress, it can leave a person feeling rejuvenated.
  • A traditional Swedish massage involves the whole body. You will begin on your stomach and flip over at the halfway point. If there are areas you wish to focus on, please let the therapist know to allocate more time for that area.

Swedish Massage vs Deep Tissue Massage

Swedish massage and deep tissue massage may be confused with one another as they share some similar techniques. However, one key difference between the two is the difference in pressure applied and the intended purpose.

For instance, a Swedish massage uses long gliding strokes and light-to-moderate pressure to stimulate the body and create gentle relaxation. On the other hand, deep tissue massage uses slower and more forceful strokes to target tensions, knots and strains deep within the muscles.

Swedish Massage vs Tui Na

Also similar in techniques, Swedish massage and Tui Na use kneading, pushing, stretching and rolling. However, a Swedish massage is frequently used to boost circulation and ease muscle tension with slower movements. Moreover, lighter pressure is often applied to encourage relaxation as well. Swedish massages can also be paired with yoga and meditation.

For Tui Na, the aim of the massage is to stimulate acupressure points and release stiffness in the body. As the techniques involved in Tui Na target acupressure points, they also deploy deeper pressure to penetrate into the deeper layers of muscle tissue. Tui Na is also used to treat various musculoskeletal conditions.

What is Swedish Massage?

As a popular form of massage therapy, Swedish massage has been widely practised to help individuals relax, reduce stress and improve circulation. Swedish Massage Techniques

There are several techniques involved in Swedish massage. From the usual stroking and kneading of massages, Swedish massage also uses gliding strokes and deep circular movements to stimulate the muscle and release any tension in the body.

1. Effleurage

To warm up the body for your massage, effleurage will be used at the start of the session. It uses smooth and gentle gliding movements — stroking, superficial effleurage, and deeper effleurage — to relax the tissues in different parts of your body. With this technique, your body will adapt to these pressured strokes and loosen any knots and remove tensions at tight spots.

However, depending on your needs, your therapist will adjust the pressure accordingly so that you’ll feel comfortable throughout the session. To soothe the muscles, effleurage will also be applied at the end of the session.

2. Petrissage

For individuals experiencing injured muscles, petrissage will be used to stretch and loosen your muscles. With a series of deeper movements such as rolling, squeezing and kneading, these techniques help to promote blood circulation within your body and massage your body tissues in a rhythmic fashion.

With the aim of deep penetration into the muscles, petrissage will involve the most extended period of time as compared to other techniques in Swedish massage.

3. Friction

Coupling alongside other techniques in Swedish massage is through the use of friction. By rubbing and massaging certain areas of the body with the thumb or fingers, this technique uses deep circular or linear movements to stimulate blood flow and break down any scar tissues. Thus, friction is best applied on joints to relieve any sore muscles and realign the muscles altogether.

4. Tapotement

The tapotement technique was derived from the words tapping and drumming. Using cupped hands, the edge of the hand or even fingers, tapotement involves tapping to relax the body and stimulate blood flow. It can also help to relax any tight muscles within the body, promote better endorphin production in the body and even aid in lymphatic drainage.

Besides usual tapping and drumming, tapotement also involves slapping, hammering, hacking and cupping to get the best results.

5. Vibration

The vibration technique is best to soothe nerves or to heal areas in the body that experiencing knots. Involving rhythmic shaking of the body, your therapist will use their palms to create a form of vibration and massage your muscles or back. In doing so, the muscles will be shaken up and relaxed. However, on smaller areas of the body such as the face, your therapist will use their fingers instead.

6. Kneading

Using their hands, as well as knuckles and fingertips, a therapist uses the kneading techniques help to release knots in the body. Pressure is applied in circular and upward motions to stimulate the muscles and reduce tension.

7. Tapping

The tapping technique, which is also known as percussion, is a technique that helps to stimulate the muscles. Through various movements such as drumming, hacking, cupping, slapping and even hammering, it helps to improve blood circulation in the body and helps you to relax. With this technique, your lymphatic drainage system is also greatly improved to boost your overall health.

8. Stretching

For individuals seeking to improve their flexibility and joint movement, a therapist can include gentle stretching movements to reduce any stiffness in the body and improve overall mobility.

9. Relaxation

Besides using light to moderate pressure on the body, accompanying tools such as music, scents and essential oil can help to increase the overall session and help you to easily relax.
